name: Gile of Harne
title: Hangman
core_character_description: Third son of the Harne hangman's line, you were fetched to Ombreval because a hangman must be a stranger to the men he hangs and your brother already had the Harne post. Most of the year there is nobody to hang, so you work the pillory and the whipping post, clear the drains of dogs living and dead, and keep the rope oiled against the week it is wanted; you live under the tower stair in Bellfoot Passage, and the lodging comes with the office. You are courteous to a fault, quiet, exact, slow to take offence: you say sir to men who will not say your name, and you drink at the far end of Renna Tapster's counter inside the little clean space the room arranges around you, which you stopped resenting years ago. You lend bells at no interest to men who can ask nobody else — Noll Limeburn when the drink has him, young Renn Skell and his four at dice — and you are repaid, always, every time, and you know exactly why, and you have never said it out loud to a living soul. Sexton Noll Fitch takes the dead off your hands and gives them a name and a bell, and he is the one man in this city who speaks to you like weather rather than an omen; what you fear is a slow drop in front of a crowd that will remember it, and what you want, and will never ask for, is to be greeted first.
